Look at docs\04-candidate-brief.md, we are ONLY looking at "G — Multiplayer race over the intranet". 
Explain to me how I could test this manually, locally on my single machine.

{"content": "1|# 04 — Candidate brief
2|
3|> This is the document handed to candidates, together with the repository.
4|> (Interviewers: remove `docs/05-interviewer-guide.md` before sharing.)
5|
6|## Welcome to FairFahren 🚕
7|
8|You have a tiny 3D driving game: a Berlin taxi in a procedurally generated city. The whole game is about 50 KB of plain JavaScript — **no assets, no libraries, no build step**. Every building, tree and street comes from one seed number.
9|
10|Your job is to **extend it**.
11|
12|## Ground rules
13|
14|1. **Stay procedural.** Do not add image, model, audio, font or data files. Generate what you need in code.
15|2. **Stay small.** `npm run size` must pass (≤ 96 KB raw, ≤ 32 KB gzip for `index.html` + `src/`).
16|3. **No dependencies.** No npm packages, no CDN scripts — on the client and on any server you write.
17|4. **Stay deterministic.** World content must come from the seeded `Rng`, never from `Math.random()`.
18|5. **Keep it green.** `npm test` passes, and new logic comes with tests where it makes sense.
19|6. Small, focused commits with meaningful messages. We will read your history.
20|
21|## Getting started (≈ 30 min)
22|
23|1. Read [03-prerequisites.md](03-prerequisites.md), run `npm start`, drive around.
24|2. Read [02-technical-specification.md](02-technical-specification.md) and skim `src/main.js` — everything is wired there.
25|3. Try `?seed=7` and the `window.fairfahren` console object.
26|
27|## Tasks
28|
29|Pick **one main task** (or the one your interviewer gave you). Bonus tasks are optional.
30|
31|### A — Taxi missions (game loop) ★★
32|Turn the sandbox into a game. Spawn a waiting passenger (procedural figure + marker) at a random sidewalk spot, drive there and stop next to them to pick up, then deliver them to a destination shown on screen. Fare depends on distance and time; show money earned.
33|*Acceptance:* pickup only below 5 km/h within 4 m; destination reachable by road; fares and positions deterministic per seed + mission number; logic unit-tested without WebGL.
34|
35|### B — Traffic lights ★★
36|Add traffic lights at crossings (a pole with red/amber/green; bonus: the East-Berlin *Ampelmännchen* built from boxes). Cycle them per crossing so perpendicular directions never show green at the same time. Detect and display red-light violations.
37|*Acceptance:* state machine is a pure, tested module; lights are visible and readable at 50 m; violation is detected when crossing the stop line on red.
38|
39|### C — Minimap & navigation ★★★
40|Draw a minimap (2D canvas overlay) of streets, river and the taxi. Build a road graph from the city data and show the shortest route to a clicked destination (A* or Dijkstra).
41|*Acceptance:* the graph respects dead-ends at the river; route updates when the taxi leaves it; graph construction and pathfinding are tested.
42|
43|### D — AI traffic ★★★
44|Add 10–30 other cars that drive along the streets in the right-hand lane, turn at crossings and stop for obstacles in front of them (including the taxi).
45|*Acceptance:* no car drives through buildings or into the river; stays at ≥ 50 FPS; behaviour deterministic per seed.
46|
47|### E — A new district ★★
48|Add a new procedural block type with Berlin character — e.g. an elevated U-Bahn line (*Hochbahn*) on a viaduct along one street with stations, or a Kreuzberg-style street with *Spätis* and coloured awnings, or the Berlin Wall remnant with a strip of land.
49|*Acceptance:* integrated into `generateCity` via its own RNG fork; colliders where needed; invariant tests extended.
50|
51|### F — Better physics & feel ★★
52|Replace the kinematic model with a simple dynamic model: tyre slip, understeer/oversteer, handbrake drifts; body roll and pitch visible on the model; impact speed shakes the camera.
53|*Acceptance:* existing physics tests still pass or are consciously updated; new tests for slip behaviour.
54|
55|### G — Multiplayer race over the intranet ★★★★
56|Turn FairFahren into a short multiplayer race for **2–4 players** on different machines in the same network.
57|
58|**Flow**
59|
60|1. **Lobby.** One player starts the game server; the others open `http://<host-ip>:<port>/` and enter a name. Everyone sees who has joined (2–4 players, a fifth is turned away). Any player can press "Start" once at least two are in.
61|2. **Track.** A straight **200 m** race on a road of the city, e.g. eastwards along *Unter den Linden* from the gate. All clients derive the same track from the shared seed (the server picks the seed). Start grid with one slot per player, no taxi overlapping another.
62|3. **Start light (*Ampel*).** A traffic light above or beside the start line runs the German sequence **red → red + amber → green**. Cars are frozen until green. Every client must switch to green at the same moment (± 100 ms), regardless of network delay. Bonus: a jump start (moving before green) gets a time penalty.
63|4. **Race.** All players see all taxis moving in real time, smoothly, with a name tag. Each taxi is distinguishable (e.g. the player number on the roof sign or a coloured stripe — procedural, no textures).
64|5. **Finish line.** A visible chequered line across the road. Crossing it records the finish time (ms precision). The server, not the client, decides the official order.
65|6. **Siegerehrung.** When all players have finished (or 30 s after the winner), show the award ceremony to everyone: a podium with steps 1–2–3 built from geometry, the taxis placed on it, a camera orbit, and a results table with names and times. Then "Nochmal" returns everyone to the start grid.
66|
67|**Rules for this task**
68|
69|- The server is plain Node (`server/`), **zero dependencies** like the rest. Use the built-in `node:http`. You choose the transport — e.g. WebSocket via the HTTP `upgrade` handshake (RFC 6455, a few dozen lines), or Server-Sent Events plus `fetch` POSTs — and justify the choice in `NOTES.md`.
70|- The server serves the game files too, so players only need one URL. It listens on all network interfaces, not only `localhost`.
71|- The size budget still applies to the client (`index.html` + `src/`). Server code does not count.
72|- Single-player mode keeps working without a server.
73|
74|**Acceptance criteria**
75|
76|- Two browser windows on one machine **and** two machines in the intranet can race each other.
77|- The race state machine (lobby → countdown → racing → finished → ceremony) is a **pure module with unit tests**, including: start rejected with fewer than 2 players, fifth player rejected, finish order by time, a player disconnecting mid-race does not block the ceremony.
78|- The track (start grid, finish line) is generated from the seed and tested: 200 m long, straight, fully on road, no collider in the way.
79|- Other taxis move smoothly at 60 FPS even though network updates arrive at ~10–20 Hz (interpolation).
80|- The message protocol is documented (message types, fields, who sends what, at which rate).
81|
82|**Scoping.** This is the biggest task. In a time-boxed take-home, a solid result for steps 1–5 with two players beats a shaky all-in version; note in `NOTES.md` what you left out and how you would add it.
83|
84|### Bonus (small, any time)
85|- Headlights toggle (`L`) and a day/night cycle in the shader.
86|- Horn (WebAudio, synthesised — no audio files).
87|- Spatial grid for collision queries + a micro-benchmark.
88|- Gamepad support.
89|- Camera that does not clip into buildings.
90|
91|## What we look for
92|
93|Clean, readable code that fits the existing style; sensible decomposition (pure logic vs. rendering); tests for logic; respecting the constraints; and being able to **explain your trade-offs**. A smaller, solid result beats a large, fragile one.
94|
95|## Hand-in
96|
97|A Git repository (or bundle) with your commits, plus a short `NOTES.md`: what you built, what you'd do next, what you'd change in the existing code, how long you spent.", "total_lines": 97, "file_size": 7763, "truncated": false, "is_binary": false, "is_image": false, "not_found": false}

2|
3|## Required
4|
5|| Tool | Version | Why |
6||---|---|---|
7|| A browser with **WebGL2** | Current Chrome, Edge, Firefox or Safari | Runs the game. Check at <https://get.webgl.org/webgl2/>. |
8|| **Node.js** | 22 LTS or newer | Dev server, unit tests (`node --test`), size check. No `npm install` needed — there are no dependencies. |
9|| Git | any | To receive and hand in the task. |
10|
11|Recommended: VS Code (or any editor) with ESLint/Prettier if you like — not required, and not part of the project.
12|
13|## Run
14|
15|```bash
16|npm start
17|```
18|
19|Then open <http://localhost:8080>. Another port: `node tools/serve.mjs 3000`.
20|
21|ES modules do not load from `file://`, so opening `index.html` directly will not work — always use the dev server (or any static server, e.g. `python -m http.server`).
22|
23|## Check
24|
25|```bash
26|npm test
27|```
28|
29|```bash
30|npm run size
31|```
32|
33|`npm run check` runs both. Both must pass before you hand in.
34|
35|## Debugging tips
36|
37|- `window.fairfahren` in the browser console gives you `city`, `car`, `camera` and the `TAXI` tuning. Example: `fairfahren.car.speed = 30` or `fairfahren.TAXI.maxSpeed = 60`.
38|- `?seed=42` in the URL generates a different city.
39|- Shader compile errors are thrown with the GLSL log — look in the console.
40|
41|## Troubleshooting
42|
43|| Symptom | Fix |
44||---|---|
45|| Black page, "WebGL2 is not available" | Enable hardware acceleration in the browser settings, or try another browser. |
46|| Blank page, module errors in the console | You opened the file via `file://`. Use `npm start`. |
47|| `node --test` finds no tests | Node too old. Use Node 22+. |

No multiplayer server exists yet in the repo (there's no `server/` dir) — so this is the manual test plan you'd run against a candidate's implementation (or your own). Everything in G can be exercised on one machine, because the brief's own first acceptance criterion accepts "two browser windows on one machine" as a valid race; the only thing a single machine can't fully prove is real cross-machine networking, which you can still partially simulate.

## 1. Setup

1. Start the server the candidate specifies (per their `NOTES.md`, e.g. `node server/server.mjs`). Note the port.
2. Confirm it's **serve + game in one** : opening `http://localhost:<port>/` should show the game itself, not a 404 or a lobby-only page.
3. Confirm it listens on all interfaces, not only localhost:
   - `netstat -ano | findstr LISTENING | findstr <port>` → local address should be `0.0.0.0:<port>` (or `[::]:`), not `127.0.0.1:<port>`.
   - Find your LAN IP (`ipconfig`, e.g. `192.168.x.x`) and `curl http://192.168.x.x:<port>/` from the same machine — this proves loopback-only isn't hiding it.
   - If you have *any* second device (phone, tablet, laptop), load `http://192.168.x.x:<port>/` on it. That gives you a genuine two-machine test with zero extra kit. Note: the first outside connection on Windows may trigger a Firewall prompt — that's part of the intranet experience and worth letting through.

## 2. Lobby (step 1 + acceptance "start rejected <2 players", "fifth player rejected")

Use **two distinct browser profiles**, not two tabs: a normal Chrome window plus an InPrivate/Incognito window (or Chrome + Firefox). A second tab in the same profile is fine visually but is the weakest test since they share `localStorage`/storage events — some implementations accidentally rely on that. Each window: enter a **different name** and confirm the name you typed is what everyone else sees.

- With 1 player: every "Start" attempt somewhere must be refused (button disabled or server rejects — check the result is consistent).
- Add more InPrivate windows until you have **5**: the fifth must be turned away with a sensible message, not silently dropped or admitted.
- With 2+ players: pressing Start in *any* window starts the race for *all* windows at once.
- Leave one player idle in the lobby >60 s while others join — no crash, no stuck state.

## 3. Track & grid (step 2 + "generated from the seed, 200 m, on road")

- The server picks the seed: load the same lobby URL in all windows and confirm every window generated the *same city* (same landmark at spawn — visually) although nobody typed `?seed=`.
- All taxis spawn in a grid, staggered slots, none overlapping or inside a building; the start line lies on a straight road segment.
- 200 m: drive the track once and judge it against a known speed (`fairfahren.car.speed` / `TAXI.maxSpeed` from `window.fairfahren`) — or at least confirm it's visibly short and straight, and that the finish line sits before any curve/collision.

## 4. Start light (step 3, the ±100 ms requirement)

This is the fiddliest one. Practical single-machine method:

- Put two windows side by side, each filling half a monitor.
- Start a screen recording at 60 fps (or use the fact that both windows are on screen at once and just watch for a visible flash of green in one before the other — anything perceptible to the eye *will* be >100 ms, so "both switch at the same instant by eye" is a pass, "I can see green in window A while B still shows red" is a hard fail).
- More precise: in both consoles, log the transition (`performance.now()` on the state change) with the race started once — compare the two delta readings across 2–3 restarts.
- Verify the full German sequence appears: **red → red+amber → green** (no separate green-after-amber-only, amber is *with* red).
- Cars frozen: mash W/S during red and red+amber — the taxi must not move.
- Bonus jump start: in one window, hold W a split second before green — that player's result should carry a time penalty (or whatever the implementer documented).

## 5. Race itself (step 4 + the interpolation criterion)

- **Smoothness**: watch the *other* windows' taxis, not your own. They should look continuous at 60 fps, never stepping/teleporting at 10–20 Hz.
- **Frequency evidence**: Chrome DevTools → Network tab → WS (or EventStream) connection → Messages. Confirm state updates arrive roughly every 50–100 ms, not every frame, and confirm the client actually interpolates between them (taxi keeps gliding between two messages).
- **Distinguishability**: every taxi shows a name tag and a per-player marker (number on roof sign or coloured stripe), all visible procedurally.
- **Self-check**: your own taxi must feel laggy-free (client-side prediction or pure local control), not rubber-banding behind the server at 10 Hz.

## 6. Finish & official order (step 5)

- A chequered line is visible at the end; crossing it stops your countdown per client and shows a time.
- Official order is the **server's** claim: does the server's message agree with your own timestamp? The interesting check is a *near-tie*: finish two windows within ~100 ms of each other by hand and verify the recorded order matches the ms-precision times shown (ms precision is visible in the results, otherwise you can't verify it at all).

## 7. Disconnect resilience (acceptance "disconnecting mid-race does not block ceremony")

- Close one racing window's process (not just switch tabs — close the whole browser).
- Remaining player: no hang, no freeze — either they finish and the ceremony still runs (with the leaver marked DNF or omitted, whatever `NOTES.md` promises), or the 30-s-after-winner timeout fires and the ceremony happens anyway.
- Also try *reconnecting* the same name while the match is live — see what happens (anything reasonable is fine; crashing is not).

## 8. Siegerehrung (step 6)

- Ceremony appears for **everyone** (not just the winner's window), 30 s after the first finisher at the latest.
- Podium steps 1–2–3 built from real geometry, taxis positioned on the right steps per final order, camera auto-orbits.
- "Nochmal" puts *all* windows back on a fresh start grid, names retained, ready for a second race — run that second race once, it's where lazy re-init bugs live.

## 9. Regression: single-player keeps working (acceptance)

- With *no* multiplayer server running, open the plain dev server (`npm start`, `http://localhost:8080`) and drive freely. No client code should force multiplayer or throw because there's no WS.

## 10. Quick automated near-checks

- `npm run check` must pass (size budget still ≤ 96 KB / ≤ 32 KB gzip, and `index.html` + `src/` only — server code excluded).
- `npm test` should include the required pure state-machine tests (start <2 players rejected, fifth rejected, finish order by time, disconnect mid-race) and track-generation tests.
- Skim `NOTES.md`: transport chosen with a justification, and the message protocol documented (types, fields, sender, rate) — that's an explicit acceptance item, and the manual test above only covers the observable part of it.

One note on what can't be cheaply tested on one machine: real ~10–50 ms network jitter between machines. The closest cheap simulation is Chrome DevTools network throttling ("Slow 3G" + latency) applied to one racing window — the other taxi should still interpolate acceptably at that latency, which is a stronger pass than two windows sitting on the same loopback.
